Display preferences work with a live preview. Live at **http://maker:4001/preferences.html** (screenshots `prototypes/shot-60-prefs-default.png` and `shot-61-prefs-large-compact.png`, the latter showing **Large text + Compact density**).

The panel offers:

- **Text size** — Small / Medium / Large, changing how large bookmark text appears (the preview reflects it immediately).
- **List density** — **Comfortable** (roomy cards with descriptions) vs **Compact** (tighter rows, more bookmarks visible at once — this is the "how many items are shown" dial you asked about).
- **Items per load** — how many bookmarks load at a time as you scroll a large library (20 / 50 / 100).
- **Default sort order** — the remembered default from earlier, gathered here with the rest.

All choices are **saved automatically** and remembered for next time (a small "✓ … saved" line confirms).

Two checks:

1. I interpreted **"how many items are shown"** two ways — a **density** toggle (compact fits more) *and* a separate **"items per load"** number. Are both useful, or did you mean just one of them?
2. Anything else you'd want under display preferences right now (for example a light/dark appearance)? — or are **text size, density, items-per-load, and default sort** the right set for this first version?
